mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registered Corporate Matters (Corporate Registry Extract, Certificate of Incorporation equivalent for a Chusik Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea via Supreme Court of Korea IROS e-Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: obtain certified court-issued corporate registry extract and seal certificate, then apply directly to the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Division. Non-member state: obtain court extract, Korean MOFA consular authentication, then destination state embassy/consulate legalization in Seoul. These paths are mutually exclusive; never chain apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of No Delinquency in National Taxes
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (Homaex Tax Portal)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: issue certificate, verify the responsible tax office signature, and obtain Korean MOFA Apostille. Non-member state: issue certificate, notarize the tax office signature if required, obtain MOFA consular authentication, and complete destination consulate legalization. Only one authentication path applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for incorporation, licensing and corporate bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public admitted before a District Court, or law office exercising notarial authority under the Notary Public Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: notarize the board resolution and signature capacity before a Korean notary, then obtain Korean MOFA Apostille. Non-member state: notarize before a Korean notary, obtain Korean MOFA consular authentication, then legalize through the embassy/consulate of the receiving state. Parallel paths; do not apply sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Chusik Hoesa Articles of Association, prepared in Korean and translated into English)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean Notary Public and Korean corporate counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: notarize the Articles of Incorporation, then obtain Korean MOFA Apostille. Non-member state: notarize the Articles, obtain Korean MOFA consular authentication, then legalize through the destination state consulate in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive authentication mechanisms.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the proposed Korean corporate account or for the foreign shareholder corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed commercial bank under Financial Services Commission supervision, or the foreign shareholder's licensed home-country banker
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private document path. Apostille Convention state: notarize the banker's signature and corporate capacity before a Korean notary, then apply for Korean MOFA Apostille. Non-member state: notarize the banker's signature, obtain Korean MOFA consular authentication, then legalize through the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul. Use only the path mandated by the receiving jurisdiction.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based enhanced due diligence must be conducted before onboarding and continuously thereafter. All counterparties, shareholders, directors, UBOs, senior management, vessels, aircraft, bill-of-lading parties, agents, and cargo interests must be screened against the UN Consolidated Security Council List, OFAC SDN List and 50% ownership rule, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK HM Treasury sanctions, and Republic of Korea sanctions lists maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. PEP screening must cover domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates. Every PEP relationship requires senior management approval, documentation of source of wealth and source of funds, enhanced ongoing monitoring, adverse media review, negative-news alerts, periodic re-screening, false-positive disposition, and retention of full AML/CFT records for at least five years after termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea IROS (Internet Registration Office, www.iros.go.kr) and Hugeso electronic incorporation portal (hugeso.scourt.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Commercial Act Article 19, the official registered corporate name must be written in Hangul and must include the liability suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' or 'Stock Company'. An English or other foreign-language trade name may be used for invoicing and banking purposes, but the IROS registry search and all government filings must rely on a congruent Hangul transliteration. The name should follow a four-tier convention: distinctive brand or business marker; regulated dangerous-goods forwarding activity descriptor; geographic or regional qualifier; and statutory stock company suffix. No bare Romanization is accepted as the official name; any English name must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul and must not materially diverge from the registered Hangul name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The IROS name-clearance result is valid for 30 days from first approval and cannot be extended as a matter of right; the applicant must either complete registration or refile before expiry. Upon rejection, obtain the registry officer's written reason and reference number. Within 14 days, submit a written reconsideration through the IROS portal attaching a comparative table of prior registered names, evidence of a distinct Hangul name, the precise ISIC 5229 dangerous-goods forwarding business scope, and any showing that the cited similar name is inactive. If reconsideration is denied, file an application for adjudication with the competent District Court under the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act, while in parallel preparing a materially different name filing to avoid further delay. Legal counsel should preserve all IROS timestamps, appeal letters and decision notices for the administrative and judicial record.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a high-risk dangerous-goods forwarding licensee, a virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address is not acceptable. The National Tax Service requires a physical head office for business registration under the Value-Added Tax Act, and the local Gu tax office will require a signed lease, premises photographs, and evidence of operational capacity. Korean banks will refuse to open and maintain a corporate account for a DG forwarder using a virtual office because the AML/KYC examination cannot verify operational substance. The transport licensing regulator, under Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries oversight, also requires on-site offices where DG declarations, safety data sheets, transport contracts, bills of lading, hazmat emergency plans, and AML/CFT compliance records are retained and accessible. Virtual office use is therefore rejected for this industry and would materially trigger enhanced bank due diligence, license refusal, and tax de-registration risk.

unannounced_inspection_checklist: Signed physical lease agreement for a term of at least 12 months at the registered address
Registered address exactly matching the business registration certificate and DG forwarding license
Visible office signage with the Korean corporate name and stock company suffix at the registered premises
Actual personnel, desks, filing cabinets, and information technology infrastructure present during business hours
Retention of DG forwarding contracts, bills of lading, safety data sheets, hazmat declarations, cargo manifests, and audit records at the registered office
Availability of the red corporate seal, corporate documents, and bank records for inspection
Adoption and on-site availability of an AML/CFT manual, UBO KYC file, PEP and sanctions screening policy, and suspicious transaction reporting procedure
physical_inspection_likelihood.quantified_risk: High. The unannounced physical inspection probability by the National Tax Service, local Gu municipal tax office, and DG transport safety authorities is estimated at 70% within the first 12 months after license activation, rising to approximately 85% if the company books air or sea dangerous-goods cargo into Korea Customs Service high-risk screening channels.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 8566, as revised), Articles 289, 290, 295, 316, 317, 318, 330, 358, 362, 363 and 409; Registration of Commercial Matters Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Article 5; International Freight Forwarding Agency Act; Aviation Safety Act; Maritime Safety Act; Chemicals Control Act; Environmental Impact Assessment Act; Occupational Safety and Health Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Office of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, operated under the Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea; online filings are accepted through the Korean Internet Registry Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation accompanied by an Incorporation Registration Application; the official extract issued by the registry is the Corporate Registration Certificate, which is the authoritative evidence of corporate existence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa, and no blocked escrow account is required for ordinary formation. However, the aggregate subscription price for initial shares must be fully credited to a domestic corporate bank account before the incorporation registration is filed. For a dangerous goods forwarding entity operating under ISIC 5229, the business is required to maintain a financial guarantee or liability insurance policy covering DG transport accidents, warehouse fire risks, environmental pollution, and chemical spills; this financial capacity requirement functions as a de facto capital-support rule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [PLACEHOLDER] CHUSIK HOESA (THE COMPANY). The undersigned directors, constituting the entire board of directors lawfully elected at the incorporation meeting, hereby waive prior notice, acknowledge that a quorum is present, and unanimously adopt the following resolutions. 1. Capital Subscription and Shares. The board ratifies the subscription and issuance of [PLACEHOLDER] ordinary shares at KRW 100 par value each, totaling KRW [PLACEHOLDER] in paid-in capital, which has been fully paid in cash into the corporate account maintained at [PLACEHOLDER] Bank. The representative director is directed to receive the subscription consideration, issue share certificates in accordance with Article 358 of the Commercial Act, and record all shareholders in the registry of shareholders. 2. Statutory Registration. The board directs the officers to prepare and file the incorporation registration under Article 317 of the Commercial Act with the Corporate Registration Office of the District Court and to obtain the corporate business registration certificate from the local National Tax Service office within the statutory period. 3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [PLACEHOLDER], Republic of Korea. The representative director is empowered to execute and deliver the lease agreement, obtain landlord consent, and submit any required notice of registered office to the registry. 4. Banking Authorization. The board approves the opening of domestic currency, foreign exchange, and letter of credit accounts at [PLACEHOLDER] Bank. The representative director and one additional director are designated as authorized signatories, jointly or severally as the bank mandate requires, for wire transfers, Swift payments, trade finance instruments, and all banking approvals. 5. Statutory Officers. [PLACEHOLDER] is appointed Representative Director, [PLACEHOLDER] is appointed Director of Dangerous Goods Compliance, and, if required by applicable law, [PLACEHOLDER] is appointed Auditor. Each officer is authorized to appear before courts, notaries, banks, tax authorities, and licensing agencies on behalf of the Company. 6. Corporate Seal. The board adopts the corporate seal specimen to be filed with the court registry, and the representative director shall serve as custodian of the seal, requiring countersignature for all dangerous goods manifests, hazardous waste consignments, and licensing submissions. 7. Insurance and Indemnification. The board authorizes the purchase of environmental liability, cargo liability, aviation and maritime dangerous goods liability, fire and pollution insurance, and may indemnify officers and directors to the maximum extent permitted by law. 8. Retention of Professionals. The board authorizes retention of attorneys, certified public accountants, licensed freight forwarding agents, and DG safety advisors to implement this resolution and all ancillary licenses. 9. Effectiveness. Each of the foregoing resolutions is effective immediately and may be implemented severally by any one officer acting on the Company's behalf. The resolutions are hereby adopted by unanimous written consent of the board of directors as of the date set forth above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, notarization and filing of the Articles of Incorporation with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registry Office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online submissions via the Korean Internet Registry Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholders shall prepare articles of incorporation containing the corporate name, object clauses covering dangerous goods forwarding, freight transport arrangement, customs brokerage, warehousing, and all ancillary activities, the total authorized shares, the par value, the amount of capital paid on incorporation, the registered office location, and the method of public notice. Each page of the articles must be paginated and sealed by the founders to prevent substitution. If any shareholder is a non-resident, the articles must be supported by notarized signatures and passport copies. The application is submitted to the court registry together with the notarized articles and payment receipts. The registry officer examines conformity with Articles 289 through 317 of the Commercial Act and, upon acceptance, assigns a corporate registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarized original Articles of Incorporation
Founders identification documents or notarized passports
Power of attorney if a founder is represented
Proof of a fixed bank account for capital subscription
Payment receipt of court registration tax and service fee
Landlord consent for the registered office, if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a demand for correction or suspension, the applicant must eliminate the stated defect within ten business days and re-file the corrected articles, paying any supplemental fee. If the registry rejects the application, a written reason must be requested, and a new application may be filed after material amendment; an administrative appeal may be filed within 90 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription payment, first board resolution, and registration of statutory officers and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registration Office of the District Court and the corporate banking department of the designated domestic bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the articles are accepted, each initial shareholder shall remit the subscription amount into a corporate bank account opened in the company name. The bank shall issue a certificate of payment. The first board of directors then meets and adopts the pro-forma resolution, which ratifies the capital payment, designates the registered office, authorizes bankers and signatories, and appoints the representative director, DG compliance director, and auditor, if any. The representative director or authorized attorney submits the resolution, the acceptance declarations of each director, and the corporate seal report to the same court registry. The registry enters the officers' names, the registered office address, and the seal specimen into the corporate register and issues the certified Corporate Registration Certificate.
required_dossiers: First board of directors resolution, original
Acceptance statements signed by each director and auditor
Corporate bank certificate of capital payment
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Application for registration of incorporation
Lease agreement or landlord consent for the registered office
Corporate seal registration report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the registry suspends the registration due to officer ineligibility or capital payment defects, the company must replace the challenged officer or submit bank-confirmed remittance details, then reapply within ten business days. If the capital payment certificate is challenged, obtain a corrected certificate from the bank and attach a transaction history; re-file with no additional registry examination fee if made within the correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration and corporate tax registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service through the Home Tax Service online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must apply for a business registration certificate within twenty business days following incorporation. The application is made to the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business. The company must submit the certified corporate registration extract, articles, corporate seal certificate, lease contract, and bank account information. For dangerous goods forwarding, the applicant should indicate the ISIC 5229 activity and attach the intended freight forwarding license information once available. The tax office will issue a business registration certificate with a corporate taxpayer identification number that is also used for VAT, wage withholding, and customs filings. The certificate must be posted at the place of business and retained for bank onboarding and licensing.
required_dossiers: Business registration application, standard form
Certified corporate registration extract
Articles of incorporation
Corporate seal certificate
Lease contract or ownership registry for the principal office
Identity document of the representative director
Bank account confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office questions the office address or business classification, provide landlord consent, a utility bill in the company name, and a revised business purpose description. The application may be corrected online within ten business days. If the registration is suspended, request a written reason and file a corrected application with the district tax office; an administrative appeal can be lodged within 90 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign investment report and capital remittance verification for non-resident shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA Invest Korea Center or the designated Foreign Exchange Bank where the capital remittance is deposited.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before issuing shares to a non-resident, the company or the non-resident shareholder shall file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The non-resident shall open a foreign currency deposit account with a domestic foreign exchange bank and remit the subscription funds through legitimate banking channels. The bank verifies the source of funds and issues a certificate of deposit. After the incorporation registration is completed, the non-resident shareholder files a report on acquisition of shares and obtains a foreign investment certificate. This certificate is required for later dividend repatriation, capital withdrawal, and conversion of capital sums. The timeline must be coordinated with the capital payment step to avoid late filing penalties.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment report form
Certified corporate registration extract or draft articles
Non-resident shareholder passport and address proof
Source of funds statement or bank anti-money-laundering clearance
Foreign currency remittance confirmation from the receiving bank
Power of attorney and corporate records if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the report is queried, submit corrected source-of-funds documentation, remittance details, and a board resolution of the company. Where the 30-day filing period has lapsed, pay the applicable non-compliance penalty and file a late report with the bank or KOTRA. Repeated rejection should be escalated to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through a formal written petition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Dangerous goods forwarding license, chemical facility approval, and fire safety clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport; Ministry of Environment through the National Institute of Chemical Safety; and the local Fire Department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following business registration, the company shall apply for the International Freight Forwarding Agency registration under the International Freight Forwarding Agency Act. The application must identify the dangerous goods commodity classes, the means of transport such as air, sea, and multimodal, and the warehouse locations. For air shipment of dangerous goods, the company must designate a dangerous goods safety advisor and comply with IATA-DGR and the Korean Aviation Safety Act. For sea shipment, the company must implement IMDG Code segregation, stowage, and documentation procedures acceptable under the Maritime Safety Act. If the company operates or controls a chemical warehouse, a chemical storage facility permit or report must be filed with the National Institute of Chemical Safety under the Chemicals Control Act, and a dangerous goods storage site fire safety permit must be obtained from the local Fire Department. The physical warehouse must undergo environmental screening before operation to determine the applicable EIA tier.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate
Corporate registration extract and corporate seal certificate
International freight forwarding agency registration application
Dangerous goods operation and safety management manual
Certificate of appointment of dangerous goods safety advisor
Warehouse layout and process safety drawings
Chemical storage facility permit or report if storage capacity threshold is met
Fire safety design document and workplace environmental risk assessment
Proof of liability insurance and financial guarantee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DG license application is suspended, the applicant must address the specified deficiency in fire suppression, ventilation, segregation, or safety advisor qualification and resubmit within 90 days. For chemical facility permit denials, a new application must include a revised process safety management plan; the applicant may also request mediation by the National Institute of Chemical Safety. Administrative appeals and court litigation are available within 90 days of any adverse decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport; Ministry of Environment through the National Institute of Chemical Safety; National Fire Agency and the local Fire Department; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Dangerous Goods International Freight Forwarding Agency Registration, together with the Dangerous Goods Transport Operator Approval issued under the Aviation Safety Act and Maritime Safety Act, and the Hazardous Chemicals Storage Facility Permit issued under the Chemicals Control Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment - Environmental Impact Assessment Division, supported by the National Institute of Chemical Safety and the Korea Environment Corporation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For a physical dangerous goods forwarding and warehousing facility, a Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment is required where the developed warehouse area exceeds 10,000 square meters or dangerous goods storage capacity exceeds the statutory threshold of 100 tons. Storage of lesser quantities requires Chemical Facility Reporting, which operates as an environmental registration under the Chemicals Control Act. A purely administrative forwarding office with no warehouse, loading, or chemical handling operations is classified as Exempt from project-level EIA but must still comply with chemical notification, emergency reporting, and workplace environmental duties.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Quantitative compliance thresholds include wastewater from washing, drip-deck, and fire water containment areas meeting effluent limits of COD not above 40 mg/L, BOD not above 30 mg/L, SS not above 40 mg/L, total nitrogen not above 30 mg/L, and total phosphorus not above 3 mg/L. VOC storage and transfer points must not exceed a pooled leak threshold of 200 ppmv under leak detection and repair inspection, and fugitive VOC controls must keep total facility emissions below 3.0 metric tons per year unless an offset or abatement permit is obtained. Hazardous waste containers must be sealed, labeled, and manifested, with disposal completed within 180 days of generation, and on-site storage limited to 10,000 kg or 30 days, whichever is shorter, unless a licensed transfer and storage facility permit is approved.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Permit for Dangerous Goods Storage Sites must be obtained from the local Fire Department, including structural load inspection and fire resistance rating certification for warehouse racks. If the site appears on the national emergency risk register, civil defense protective compliance is mandatory. KOSHA approval requires on-site workplace environmental measurement and dangerous goods handling approval, and the emergency response and spill containment plan must be approved by the local Fire Department and the Ministry of Environment office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Customs and export declarations are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that establishes a Chusik Hoesa or a foreign corporation domestic place of business in Korea must register with the National Tax Service through the HomeTax portal. The legal representative submits: (1) certificate of incorporation or certified copy of the foreign company register, (2) Korean business license for dangerous goods freight forwarding (ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510) issued by the competent ministry, (3) domestic place-of-business lease contract and proof of fixed premises, (4) appointment of a domestic tax representative if the head office is outside Korea, and (5) power of attorney. Under the Value-Added Tax Act, the business registration is simultaneously a VAT registration; the NTS issues a 10-digit business registration number (Korean TIN) used for corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding. Registration must be completed before commencing taxable supplies; a foreign corporation solely earning domestic-source income without a fixed place may use a surrogate tax representative for identification rather than holding a domestic VAT-registered place of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not operate a check-the-box or elective pass-through classification system. A Chusik Hoesa is taxed as a domestic corporate resident. Hybrid mismatch rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act and OECD Multilateral Instrument positions apply to deny mismatches; no domestic entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for corporations: every Chusik Hoesa making VAT taxable supplies is mandatorily registered as a general taxpayer. Simplified taxpayer status (KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover) is not available to corporations or freight forwarders; dangerous goods forwarding is a taxable service subject to the standard 10% rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All corporations must issue electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoice) via the NTS HomeTax real-time electronic invoice system for every taxable supply, transmit the e-Tax Invoice data to the NTS by the day following issuance, and include the mandatory VAT invoice identifier. Large-enterprise and ERP integration are done through the HomeTax e-invoice API; paper tax invoices are generally prohibited for corporations. The NTS performs real-time data matching and anti-fraud risk scoring. Export transactions are reported through KCS UNI-PASS and matched to the zero-rated VAT schedules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT is available under Article 24 of the Value-Added Tax Act for exported goods and for services in direct connection with the export or import of goods, including international freight transport, freight forwarding, brokerage, and customs clearance services supplied to a foreign person. For a DG/Hazmat freight forwarder, zero-rating requires proof that the logistics services were part of an export transaction and that payment is received from abroad or settled in foreign currency. Purely domestic movement of dangerous cargo within Korea does not qualify for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Confirmation) filed through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight showing matching shipper, consignee, and cargo description
Commercial Invoice and packing list for the underlying exported goods
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing final receipt of export sales proceeds in foreign currency
Dangerous Goods Declaration under IMDG Code or IATA DGR, together with the valid Hazardous Materials Transport License for the DG forwarding scope
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and KCS jointly inspect export zero-rating claims. An unlawful zero-rating claim triggers additional VAT at the standard rate plus additional taxes of 20% for negligent misstatement and 40% for fraudulent misrepresentation, with interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Criminal referral is possible for forged export declarations, bills of lading, or foreign exchange settlement certificates, leading to imprisonment and fines under the Customs Act and the Value-Added Tax Act. The statutory audit period is extended to six years for such cases, and clawbacks are retrospective to the original filing period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), exercising delegated regulatory authority with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, is the central bank and administrative supervisor of South Korea's foreign exchange clearance, reporting, and KRW convertibility system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized current-account system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, while capital-account transactions are conditionally open through a registration-and-filing mechanism rather than blanket BOK permission. For a Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in dangerous-goods air and sea forwarding, non-resident shareholders are permitted, but inbound equity capital must be reported to the designated foreign exchange bank and should be booked through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act route if the capital constitutes foreign direct investment. Profit remittances, including dividends and liquidation proceeds, are generally remittable through a domestic bank after corporate income tax and withholding tax clearance, supported by audited financial statements and board resolutions. There is no mandatory surrender of all export proceeds into KRW, but exporter-received foreign currency is required to be collected within a prescribed statutory period and is normally housed in a domestic foreign-currency account. Increased surveillance applies to high-risk sectors such as hazardous-materials forwarding, where banks must verify physical trade documents, DG licenses, and consignee chains in the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system. Overall convertibility is therefore unrestricted for genuine trade and investment flows, with the BOK and MOEF monitoring high-risk channels through the Korea FX Information System and requiring transaction-level purpose codes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Korea Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related BOK foreign exchange regulations, export proceeds from cargo, freight forwarding, or logistics services must be collected within 180 days from the date of export declaration or service completion, unless an extension is approved by the designated foreign exchange bank for legitimate commercial reasons. There is no mandatory conversion ratio for commercial export earnings; Korean exporters may retain the funds in domestic foreign-currency accounts, provided the proceeds are recorded in the Korea Foreign Exchange Information System and the underlying export entry has been reported through UNI-PASS. If the amount is collected after the statutory timeline, the remittance must be settled with the foreign exchange bank, and the bank must report the delinquency status to the BOK supervisory framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Dangerous-Goods Freight Forwarding Operational Currency Account
Foreign-Direct-Investment Capital Escrow and KRW Operating Account
Trade Settlement Escrow Account with LC and Collection Services
Cross-Border Payment and Export Proceeds Foreign-Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore non-bank electronic money institutions and digital EMIs are not viable as primary treasury custodians for this entity. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, an EMI cannot maintain domestic KRW accounts, issue Korean IBAN equivalents, provide foreign-currency deposit services, or execute cross-border payments without a licensed domestic bank intermediary and BOK/MOEF registration. Several licensed fintech remittance providers exist in Korea, but they act as money-transfer aggregators and are prohibited from servicing a High-Risk_Dangerous_Goods corporate account with LC, documentary collection, and FX hedging needs. The legal constraint is decisive: the treasury structure must remain with a commercial banking counterparty; fintech EMIs may be used only as a supplementary collection rail for small parcel customs fees, never for escrow or trade disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or supervised video-call presence is mandatory for the statutory representative and the ultimate beneficial owners when the corporate risk tier is High_Risk_Special_License. The Korean Commercial Code and Real Name Financial Transaction Act require verification of the registered corporate address, director authority, and beneficial-ownership chain. Remote consular proxy opening is possible for non-resident representatives only by power of attorney apostilled and notarized at the Korean consulate, but the local commercial bank reserves the right to require an in-branch interview before issuing green-listed FX limits or activating trade rails. For DG-forwarding profiles, at least one Korean-resident or visiting officer of the entity must appear for a live interview and sign the high-risk customer acceptance form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between stated logistics activity and actual account inflows from non-resident third parties before any cargo is declared
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly stamped corporate registry, board resolution appointing treasury signatories, shareholder registry and beneficial ownership declarations, 12-month source-of-funds bank statements for all equity investors, notarized shareholder loan agreements if funds are supplied as intercompany loans, and a funds-flow description showing the economic rationale of every pre-trade remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dangerous goods licensing and cargo documentation mismatch causing sanctions red flags at the bank's autonomous transaction monitoring layer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export and import declarations, IATA/UN dangerous-goods declarations, IMDG Dangerous Goods Transport Document or Shipper's Declaration for sea freight, valid hazardous-material transport permit, freight forwarding contracts, principal shipping documents, and shipper safety data sheets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or counterparty overlap with SDN, UN, or Korean FSS sanctions lists coupled with passenger-vessel or phantom air-cargo partnerships
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Open-source screening results from BOK/FSS/FATF-sanction databases, U.S. OFAC and UN consolidated lists, actual vessel and aircraft utilisation logs, charter agreement with cargo operator, head-office due-diligence reports for all overseas correspondents, and attestation that the DG forwarder accepts no military dual-use cargo without a separate export-control license.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice or payment mismatch between freight forwarder service fees and high-value settlements to shell logistics entities in lower-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of master service agreements, corresponding hazardous-goods handling invoices, packing lists and weight tickets from the physical warehouse, proof of insurance for dangerous-goods liability, treasury payment ledger matched to bank purpose codes, and China/US/EU/Korean jurisdictional business-registration extracts for each beneficiary in the disbursement chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity for the Korean Chusik Hoesa must be routed through a designated Korean foreign-exchange bank using the Foreign Investment Promotion Act route when a non-resident shareholder subscribes to shares. The remitting bank should originate a SWIFT MT103 with a standing instruction to credit the Chusik Hoesa capital-escrow account, and the receiving bank must report the transaction in the Korea Foreign Exchange Information System using the foreign-investment equity capital purpose code. The bank will issue a foreign currency purchase or KRW conversion advice at the spot market rate once the BOK/MOEF foreign investment registration information has been validated. If instead the injection is an intercompany working-capital loan or trade-related advance, the remittance must be classified under the relevant current-account purpose code and supported by a written loan agreement. A Korean registered public accountant must later perform capital verification by comparing the actual received FX amount, the converted KRW balance, the share registers, and the BOK file number before the company can distribute any dividend or repatriate the injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for service fees, port handling, air freight terminal charges, sub-agent commissions, and DG insurance premiums, provided each payment is documented with a contract and invoice and submitted through the corporate internet banking payer portal. For high-value purchase of logistics equipment or charter capacity, a commercial letter of credit should be opened at Woori/Hana/Shinhan/KB against a draft and transport documents covering the dangerous-goods moving chain; documentary collections are acceptable when a future or long-term forwarding counterparty is financially strong and the underlying cargo documents are processed under the Uniform Rules for Collections. Korea requires the reporting bank to transmit transaction-level data through the FX Information System, including remittance purpose codes and relation to the approved business license, before the clearing rail is activated. Payments to foreign airlines and ocean carriers may also be effected through MT202/MT199 only under a bilateral treasury agreement; from a compliance standpoint all settlement must be attributable to a valid cargo reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Corporate USD/KRW forward contracts evidenced by underlying export invoices, import payables, or operational FX exposure arising from the dangerous-goods forwarding business
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) hedging where the onshore bank or its offshore affiliate confirms a physical or non-deliverable settlement with no speculative position

Cross-currency swap limited to matching the maturity of foreign-investment equity capital or trade-loan principal and interest in USD/KRW, purchased only where both legs are fully documented by the treasury and external auditor

Currency swap transactions exceeding 12 months are permissible only after a new BOK/MOEF capital-account filing and internal credit approval, and are generally not recommended for a stage-4 DG cash-flow ring unless a fixed asset or long-term receivable is present

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular General Meeting of Shareholders and adoption of annual financial statements (Commercial Act Art. 365)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of the Chusik Hoesa; minutes and financial statements retained and made available for shareholder and creditor inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after each fiscal-year close; for a calendar-year entity, not later than 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to call or convene the regular general meeting are exposed to administrative fines up to KRW 20,000,000; a shareholder may apply to the court for an order to convene the meeting; a continued deadlock may lead to court-ordered dissolution under the Korean Commercial Act. No automatic administrative strike-off, but failure to maintain corporate formalities may be used as evidence of non-existence of the registered office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (tax base return with attached audited or unaudited financial statements; transfer pricing disclosures where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of the unpaid corporate tax (20% for deliberate understatement and 40% for fraudulent concealment) plus daily delinquency interest of 0.025% on arrears; persistent non-filing and non-payment permit NTS compulsory collection, asset seizure, criminal referral, and tax clearance blocks before liquidation or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surtax return (10% surcharge on corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax authority through the local taxation integrated e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax return: by 31 March for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment triggers additional local tax of 10% of the unpaid surtax and daily delinquency interest of 0.025%; continued delinquency leads to compulsory collection and enforcement against corporate bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-quarter filing windows: Q1 by 25 April; Q2 by 25 July; Q3 by 25 October; Q4 by 25 January of the next fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false VAT filings attract an additional tax equal to 10% of the unpaid VAT (20% for failure based on false invoices), plus 0.025% daily delinquency interest; repeated violations can lead to NTS compulsory collection, revocation of tax clearance, and enforcement barriers to corporate dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent external audit report and audited annual financial statements, if the company is subject to mandatory external audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the regular general meeting (by 31 March for a calendar-year company); the audit report must be filed with DART within two weeks after shareholder approval of the financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-appointment of an external auditor or obstruction of the audit can trigger criminal fines and imprisonment of responsible directors under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; FSS may issue corrective orders, impose administrative sanctions, and potentially restrict dividend distributions or asset disposal until the audit is completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual dangerous-goods transport operator declaration and licence validity maintenance for DG forwarding / hazardous chemical freight
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries for sea dangerous-goods carriage; Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport for air dangerous-goods operation approvals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year revalidation and safety-transport report ordinarily due by 31 January following the reporting year; also on the licence-anniversary cycle set by the granting authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating DG forwarding without valid annual declaration or operator approval causes immediate suspension of dangerous-goods cargo handling, administrative fines under the Maritime Safety Act and Aviation Safety Act, port/airport cargo stop-orders, and possible revocation of the special statutory licence; a revoked licence terminates the lawful business purpose and opens the path to court-ordered dissolution or administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent certified audit is required under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies where (i) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are at least KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million); (ii) the stock corporation is listed on a Korean securities exchange; (iii) the company has issued securities or debt instruments through a public offering in the preceding three years; or (iv) the Financial Services Commission designates the company as one requiring public or creditor protection. For a DG freight forwarding Chusik Hoesa, a higher-risk special licence holder, financial institutions and the DG licensing authority may also impose an audit as a contractual or prudential condition even below the statutory threshold. Turnover and headcount alone do not trigger the Korean statutory audit obligation, but they are considered in the Financial Services Commission designation analysis.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) is mandatory for listed companies, financial institutions, and large designated enterprises; non-listed Chusik Hoesa companies generally apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) unless they elect K-IFRS. Small unlisted companies may use the simplified SME accounting framework exclusively for companies not otherwise subject to a mandatory external audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not operate a single annual UBO electronic register for all Chusik Hoesa companies. Under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions, the Specific Financial Information Act, and AML requirements for high-risk DG freight forwarders, financial institutions must identify and verify the ultimate beneficial owner, generally any natural person controlling 25% or more of shares or exercising ultimate management control, at account opening, at each Swift wire or letter-of-credit transaction, and when a control change occurs. For foreign investment governed by the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign investor acquiring 10% or more of voting shares or real management control must make a foreign investment report, and any subsequent change in the foreign holding or ownership structure must be reported to the competent investment authorities within 30 calendar days. Domestic share transfers do not require a 30-day government filing merely as share transfers, but must be entered in the register of shareholders; a change that affects a DG licence condition in the dangerous-goods forwarder approval may require the DG authority's post-notice or prior approval.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Statutory Auditors or Audit Committee
Register of Charges, collateral securities and pledges, where such exist
Minute book of shareholders' general meetings
Minute book of board of directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,800 per annum for a registered office address, resident corporate secretary, and compliance calendar administration in Seoul or Busan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 45,000 per annum for a mandatory independent audit by a Korean CPA firm; a smaller below-threshold DG forwarder may pay USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 for a voluntary financial statement review or agreed-upon procedures engagement.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax top marginal bracket plus 10% local income tax surtax on national tax, resulting in a combined top marginal rate of 26.4%; lower national tax brackets are 9%, 19%, and 21% before surtax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General incentives under the Special Cases Tax Limitation Act and Tax Incentive Limitation Law include R&D tax credits (up to 30-50% for SMEs), facility investment credits, job creation credits, and Free Economic Zone / Foreign Investment Zone incentives; qualifying high-tech foreign investments may receive a 5-year 100% and next 2-year 50% exemption from national and local corporate income taxes. There is no general patent box regime in Korea, but certain technology-transfer income may qualify for tax deferral or credits. Dangerous-goods DG freight forwarding under ISIC 5229 is not automatically incentive-eligible unless the activities are performed in a designated free economic zone and meet the statutory investment and technology thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (CIT Form 1: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Payment Return) together with CIT Form 2 (Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement), tax reconciliation schedules, foreign tax credit schedule, and transfer-pricing disclosure schedules; filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal, including UTX/EDI for foreign corporate filers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a semi-annual interim prepayment is required by August 31 for the first half and by February 28/29 for the second half where prior-year corporate tax liability exceeds the statutory threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within exactly three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the return is due by March 31 of the following year, with an extension of up to one month available upon advance application for reasonable cause and, for foreign corporations, an additional extension where foreign-source documentation is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report worldwide operating revenue of the Korean legal entity or, for a non-resident corporation with a Korean permanent establishment (PE), only revenue effectively connected with and attributable to that Korean PE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Chusik Hoesa DG forwarding entity, include freight forwarding service fees, dangerous-goods handling surcharges, air/sea transport commissions, hazmat documentation fees, and terminal charges. If the company acts as an intermediary rather than principal, report only net agency commissions; do not book pass-through carrier costs as revenue unless the company is legally the principal. Non-resident corporations must exclude foreign-source income that is not attributable to the Korean PE. Korean dependent-agent PE exposure arises if an offshore parent uses a Korea-based agent to negotiate or conclude DG forwarding contracts in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct direct costs incurred to produce the DG forwarding revenue: line-haul fees, air and sea carrier freight, hazmat packaging, DG safety equipment, insurance, terminal handling, customs examination, and subcontractor haulage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to foreign related parties for DG transport, freight capacity, and handling must be supported by written arm's length agreements, invoices, evidence of actual service, and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation when the statutory threshold is met. Inflated COGS is a classic Korean transfer-pricing red flag; NTS may reprice the transaction, disallow excess expense, recharacterize the excess as a constructive dividend or capital contribution, and impose 22% withholding plus fraud penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 1 minus Box 2; gross profit from licensed hazardous-goods forwarding activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the National Tax Service adjusts related-party freight rates or hazmat handling charges to the arm's length price, the resulting increase in gross profit must be reflected in the taxable return in the same or adjusted year. A non-resident corporation cannot rely on a DTA business-profits article to exclude Korean-source DG forwarding profit unless the profit is attributable to a Korean PE and the PE has economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses including salaries for the DG safety manager, rent, depreciation of DG warehouse and rolling stock assets, marketing, insurance, IT systems, and hazmat compliance training.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign corporation with a Korean PE, head-office expenses are deductible only to the extent attributable to the Korean PE and supported by an allocation method that reflects actual economic cost. Fines for DG safety violations, political donations, entertainment expenses over statutory limits, and expenses not related to the Korean business are non-deductible. The DG forwarding entity must have real rent, real employees, and real safety operations; notional or shell-company expenses will be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 3 minus Box 4; operating profit before non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean operating income must include all dangerous-goods forwarding consideration derived from services performed in Korea, including export/import freight forwarding, origin and destination handling, and local drayage. Where an offshore principal merely pays invoices while all commercial functions such as hazmat classification, carrier contracting, and route control occur in Korea, the Korean operation will be treated as a PE or the principal, and the entire Korean-sourced profit will be taxed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Includes interest income, dividend income, FX gains and losses, commissions, asset impairment, and non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends, interest, and royalties received by a non-resident corporation's Korean PE are taxed through the PE; if such income is paid directly to the head office and no PE exists, Korea imposes final withholding tax and no annual CIT return is required. Intercompany debt funding to a DG subsidiary must respect Korea's thin-capitalization rule: debt from a foreign controlling shareholder generally cannot exceed three times equity for non-financial companies (six times for financial companies); excess interest is non-deductible and may be recharacterized as constructive dividend subject to 22% WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating income plus non-operating income less non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident DG forwarder must not include or offset foreign-source passive income unless it is attributable to the Korean PE. Avoid the common error of treating international sea/air transport profit as purely foreign-source; Korea's VAT and CIT treatment of Korean-sourced international transport effectively connected to a PE follows DTA shipping/air transport articles, but income earned on inland Korean legs and ancillary DG terminal services remains taxable in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Tax Reconciliation: Additions and Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile financial ordinary income to taxable income by adding back non-deductible reserves, fines, entertainment excess, excessive compensation, and disallowed transfer-pricing adjustments; subtract non-taxable income, tax-exempt reserves, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back hazmat safety penalties, bribes, and expenses supported by inadequate documentation; include transfer-pricing secondary adjustments and thin-capitalization interest disallowance. If a treaty exemption is claimed on Korean-sourced fees, the claim must be timely and supported by a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration; otherwise the 22% final withholding tax becomes the final tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax base after tax adjustments and statutory loss carryforward deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward in Korea is 10 years for corporate tax purposes, subject to continuity-of-business and ownership limitations. A non-resident parent's foreign losses cannot be used to reduce a Korean subsidiary's or PE's taxable income; Korean PE profit is computed on a standalone arm's length basis using the OECD recognized approach and Korea's tax accounting rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Tax Computed at Statutory Rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate national corporate tax at graduated rates and add 10% local corporate income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a Korean PE are taxed at the same graduated rates as domestic corporations; there is no reduced non-resident rate for PE business income. Maintain a separate calculation of the local income tax surtax because local tax authorities may independently impose failure-to-pay penalties if the surtax is underreported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Tax Credits, Foreign Tax Credit, and Treaty Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim domestic tax credits for R&D, facility investment, foreign investment, and employment, foreign tax credits for foreign-source income included in the Korean tax base, and treaty-derived reductions or exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean PE earns foreign-source DG transport income from cross-border legs and pays foreign taxes, claim a foreign tax credit capped at the Korean CIT attributable to that foreign-source income, with no refund for excess foreign credit. Treaty benefits require a valid Tax Residency Certificate, a statement of beneficial ownership, and confirmation that the income is not attributable to the claimant's Korean PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Interim Prepayments and Balance Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct semi-annual interim corporate tax prepayments made during the year; declare final balance of national corporate tax and local surtax due with the annual return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign corporation's Korean PE must make interim prepayments whenever prior-year CIT liability exceeded the statutory exemption threshold; failure to prepay triggers daily late-payment interest and delinquency penalties. The final balance is due no later than the filing due date without a separate billing; directors who knowingly dissipate assets before this balance is paid expose themselves to corporate-veil piercing and personal collection measures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late non-filing of the annual CIT return triggers a non-filing penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid tax plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022% per day until payment. Underreporting without fraud attracts a 10% penalty; fraudulent underreporting or overstating deductible expenses attracts a 40% penalty. Failure to prepare and submit transfer-pricing contemporaneous documentation can result in NTS adjustment and a separate penalty of up to KRW 100 million. Failure to pay interim prepayments triggers daily late interest. Fraudulent tax evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 9, carrying imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax; if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, imprisonment of up to 10 years is possible.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% consisting of 20% national dividend withholding tax plus 10% local income
